terra.problem: The text says the earth is illuminated, not that the whole earth sees the angel coming.
The text does not say the angel wants everybody to hear him or that nobody has to ask him to repeat himself.
The text says the merchants grew wealthy, but does not say nobody is checking for loose change.
Staying close does not necessarily mean sharing in what is coming. The voice calls them out so they will not share in her sins or contract her plagues.
Babylon says she will never see grief, but the text does not say she thinks nothing bad is coming.
The plagues come in one day; the text does not say they all arrive at once.
The joke about the kings not having a good day makes light of their weeping over the fire consuming Babylon.
A different group is told to rejoice later, but the text does not say that crowd cheers.
The text does not say the kings make no move toward Babylon. It also gives them words to cry out, not just weeping.
The text describes the kings standing at a distance; it does not say everybody who lived in luxury with Babylon is watching from afar.
No one is left to buy the merchants' cargo, but the text does not say all their business is gone.
The text does not mention a dispute over a bill; it does not establish that nobody is having one.
The text does not say the merchants cannot let go of their picture of Babylon.
The explanation states that they are stunned and gives a reason for that feeling. Neither is stated in the text or marked as Papa Dorin's guess.
The text says those with ships were enriched by Babylon's wealth, not that all the sea folk made their living from her.
The text connects the ship owners' enrichment with their lament, but does not explicitly say that is why they weep.
The text names particular groups standing at a distance; it does not say everyone who gained from Babylon watches from afar.
The text does not place the mourners down on earth or say both groups are looking at Babylon's fall.
The saints, apostles and prophets are told to rejoice; the text does not say they are already rejoicing.
The text does not say the stone stays in one piece.
The angel says no craftsmen will be found in Babylon again, not that nobody at all is left to work there.
The text does not describe the bride and bridegroom's voices as gentle.
The passage says the nations were deceived by Babylon's sorcery; it does not say her greatness as a whole rested on it.
The text says the nations were deceived, not that nobody got better.
The text says the nations were deceived; it does not say they were not blessed or that the sorcery did them no good.
